name: Sparkline
intent: A trend small enough to sit in a table cell or on a tile: the shape of the last few periods, with no axes and no numbers.
usage: Use Sparkline where a row or a tile needs the shape of a trend beside its number, like credits used a day next to the month's total. It is one component: pass label and values. kind draws it as a line, a filled area or small bars. size goes sm (16px), md (24px), lg (32px); the width fills the container, so in a Table it fills its column. showLast picks the end out: a dot on a line, or the last bar at full strength while the rest step back. The scale fits the values it has, so a flat run sits on the middle line. It has no axes, grid, legend or tooltip on purpose: for a chart people read values off, use LineChart or BarChart. See contracts/sparkline.json for the full contract.

label.note: Names the trend for screen readers, like Credits used. A sparkline has no visible title.

values.note: The points, oldest first. One value draws as a single dot.

kind.note: A line for a rate or a level, an area when the size under the line matters, bars for counts a period.

intent.note: The colour. Without it the trend takes the first of the kit's series order, pink; red is the danger colour and is never handed out.

size.note: How tall the drawing is: 16px in a dense cell, 24px in a row, 32px on a tile.

showLast.note: Picks the end of the trend out: a dot on a line or an area, the last bar at full strength with the rest stepped back.

showBaseline.note: Lines and areas only: a faint line along the floor, so a flat run still reads as a trend.

format.note: How the first and last value read in the screen-reader summary. Nothing is written on the drawing.

currency.note: The currency code for format currency.

emptyLabel.note: What the cell says in place of the drawing when there are no values.

useWhen: A trend beside a number in a table row or a DataGrid cell, like usage a day next to the month's total.
The shape of the last few periods on a Scoreboard tile or a Card.
A list of accounts where each row's own trend matters more than its exact values.
doNot: Do not use it as the chart on a page. Use LineChart or BarChart.
Do not use it on a Scoreboard tile. A Scoreboard card draws its own trend: pass chart.points on the item.
Do not use it as a gauge or a share of a limit. Use Meter (shape circle or semicircle).
Do not use it where people need to read values off it. It has no axes and no tooltip on purpose.
Do not pass more than one series. One row, one trend; for several series use LineChart.
Do not pair it with its own legend or title. The row or tile around it already names it.
Do not draw it with loose SVG. Use this component.
Do not use raw hex; pick an intent.
a11y: An image named by label, with the first and last value in its name, like Credits used: 40 to 92, so the trend is not lost on a screen reader.
The drawing is hidden from screen readers; the same summary sits in the row as visually hidden text.
Colour is never the only carrier: the row or tile around the sparkline holds the number it belongs to.
No motion, so nothing to turn off.
